summary: An 80-foot Aermotor LS-40 in Henry County, still state-owned but surrounded by private land; build date unknown.

access.note: Still owned by the state but surrounded by private property; the register describes no public access route.

events.note: Listed on the Division's 1976 tower list as district-tower 8-6, under the name Nelson; link to Puryear not confirmed
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register on February 2, 2023

evidence.quote: This is a 80ft Aermotor LS-40 tower.
Administered by Tennessee Division of Forestry
two of the most widely constructed fire lookout tower types utilized by the TDF: the Aermotor Model LS-40 and the Aermotor Model MC-39

evidence.supports: LS-40 steel cab seven feet square, inside stairway
evidence.quote: The LS-40 is characterized by a 7-foot by 7-foot steel cab, and an internal stairway that runs back and forth between two elevations of the tower.

evidence.supports: design based on USFS specs and Aermotor windmill plans
evidence.quote: The tower design was based on the USFS specifications, and standardized plans adapted from Aermotor windmills

evidence.supports: TDF resumed construction after WWII until about 1970
evidence.quote: Following the end of World War II, the TDF resumed construction of fire lookout towers utilizing both the Aermotor LS-40 and MC-39 models until ca. 1970.
Numbers in the table (e.g., 4-7) are state forest tower numbers (district-tower) from 1976 list of towers

evidence.supports: state owns tower, private land surrounds it
evidence.quote: The tower is still owned by the state but it's surrounded by private property.

evidence.supports: many towers removed, most locations private
evidence.quote: Many have been removed, and most locations are now private property

evidence.supports: no visit suggested because land is private

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says Puryear Fire Tower; Tennessee Landforms lists Nelson in Henry County at 623 ft (the register gives 627 ft). The record links the two, but nothing read confirms they are one tower.

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933 to 1975 (National Register multiple property documentation form)

notes_for_editor: Built date is unknown in the register and was not found elsewhere: two searches, a Wikipedia check of Puryear, and the Paris Post-Intelligencer town history (no tower mention). The Puryear to Nelson link rests on county and elevation (627 ft vs 623 ft) and is not confirmed. A text search of the March 26, 2014 extant-tower table in the NRHP multiple property document found no Puryear or Nelson entry, so the tower may have been missing, rebuilt, or unlisted in 2014; a human should check the full table. The 80 ft figure is the register's tower height, so no height_m was entered because cab-floor height is not given. No staffing or fire history was found; the access level 'restricted' is an editorial reading of 'surrounded by private property'.
